newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Jan 27.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's The Wall Street Journal:
* CVS Corp is in talks to acquire Revco D.S. Inc but it is uncertain whether a deal will be completed.
* About 4,300 workers at General Motors' truck assembly plant in Ohio go on strike.

* A federal judge in Delaware has decided that the bankruptcy court there does not have the automatic right to hear business-reorganization cases, leading some to question what effect the move may have on the Chapter 11 case of Marvel Entertainment Group Inc.
* The AFL-CIO is targeting Las Vegas for one of its largest organizing drives in recent history.

* Retail prices for some vegetables have risen as much as 33 percent in Florida because of a winter freeze in that state, and some economists say other parts of the country could feel similar effects soon.
* The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp could soon settle gross-negligence charges against House Judiciary Committee Chairman Henry Hyde and 11 other former directors of a failed Chicago savings & loan.

* Seven of 12 states in the South have cut or are about to cut their unemployment insurance taxes by hundreds of millions of dollars in the belief that the U.S. economy has progressed beyond yesteryear's boom-and-bust cycles.
* New York hospitals are trying to keep alive a controversial federal-loan program for ailing hospitals that some officials want to eliminate.
* Global growth in the personal computer slowed in the fourth quarter to 11 percent. Although fourth quarter growth in the U.S. was stronger, at 15 percent, it was below a 20 percent forecast.
* Some economists believe existing home sales for December will fall 0.2 percent from that of November.

* The fourth-quarter employment cost index, scheduled to come out Tuesday, will be closely watched because of recent comments from Federal Reserve officials and Friday's rise of 30-year Treasury yields to 6.88 percent.
* Tokyo stocks dropped sharply Monday to close at 17,334.90.
* Monday's Heard on the Street and Credit Market columns were not immediately available.
* There's a new kid on the bond-market block, and it's getting harder to ignore him.

Despite recent worries that a slowdown in the purchase of U.S. Treasury securities by Japan will cripple bonds, the market's focus is beginning to shift to another Asian power - China. Bond traders and analysts say Chinese investments are more important to the stability of the bond market, and interest rates, than ever before. And some worry that a slowdown in Chinese investments could add a destabilizing factor to the U.S. capital markets in the years ahead. --Credit Markets.

* Investors in this bull market have thrown great gobs of money at highflying, acquisition-hungry companies in fashionable industries ranging from auto dealerships to wireless communications. But as the case of MobileMedia shows, that money in the wrong hands can evaporate almost overnight. -- Heard on the Street.
